claim_en: The serpent's PRE-CURSE state is itemized as the baseline that gen_11's curses will revoke: it stood erect like a reed, it HAD LEGS, it was camel-like in stature, and it was intended to be king over every beast and to eat the food of man. The measure-for-measure rule is stated on it - what it sought is withheld and what it held is revoked - and its MOTIVE is explicit at the tannaitic seat: it sought to kill the man and marry the woman. 'The greater the cunning, the greater the curse': the downfall is proportional to the stature.

check.note: A baseline state itemized so the later revocations have something to revoke.

middah: plain (the pre-curse state itemized; measure for measure, E27, stated on it)

claim_en: The serpent's speech is given its recorded content and its law-name. CONTENT: the slander that God ate from the tree and created the world, 'for every craftsman hates his competitor', with the ladder that what comes later dominates what came earlier. LAW-NAME: it is the FIRST SLANDERER, and 'it breached the fence of the world' - the third tongue kills three. A grammar defence is recorded beside it on our 3:5: the participle יֹדֵעַ (yodea, 'knowing') is SINGULAR in the ink, refuting a plural reading from the verse's own letters.

check.note: Speech content, its legal classification, and a grammatical defence read off the ink. Rides standing claim G10-07's verified defective spelling of yodea.
